label: Birds of prey are unprolific, except the kestrel
claim: Birds of prey (birds with crooked talons) lay few eggs, except the kestrel, which is the most prolific of them and lays four eggs or occasionally more.
quote: All birds of prey, or birds with crooked talons, are unprolific, except the kestrel: this bird is the most prolific of birds of prey; as many as four eggs have been observed in the nest, and occasionally it lays even more.
scope: Birds of prey (raptors); kestrel (Falco tinnunculus)
measurable_quantities: clutch size across raptor species
kestrel clutch size relative to other raptors
candidate_data: Amniote Life-History Database and the Animal Diversity Web give clutch size by species; AVONET gives body size for controlling it.

label: The hoopoe is the only self-hatching bird that builds no nest
claim: Of all birds that hatch their own eggs, the hoopoe alone builds no nest at all: it lays its eggs in a hollow tree trunk without making any nest.
quote: Of all birds that hatch for themselves the hoopoe is the only one that builds no nest whatever; it gets into the hollow of the trunk of a tree, and lays its eggs there without making any sort of nest.
scope: Hoopoe (Upupa epops) compared with all other incubating birds
measurable_quantities: presence or absence of nest construction across bird species
hoopoe nest-site structure
candidate_data: Species accounts in Birds of the World and the Animal Diversity Web record nest type; no single open trait database covers nest construction for all birds.

label: Eggs of water birds have proportionally more yolk and less white
claim: The eggs of birds that frequent rivers and marshes have a larger proportion of yolk and a smaller proportion of white than the eggs of land birds.
quote: the eggs of waterbirds have comparatively more of the yellow or yolk and less of the white
scope: Waterbirds (river and marsh birds) versus land birds
measurable_quantities: yolk and albumen mass fractions of eggs by species and habitat
candidate_data: Egg-composition measurements are compiled in the comparative literature (for example Sotherland and Rahn 1987 on the composition of bird eggs); no single open database is known.

label: Long pointed eggs are female and rounder eggs are male
claim: The shape of a bird's egg shows the sex of the chick: long, pointed eggs are female, and eggs that are round, or more rounded at the narrow end, are male.
quote: Long and pointed eggs are female; those that are round, or more rounded at the narrow end, are male.
scope: Birds' eggs, in the common hen in particular
measurable_quantities: egg shape indices (elongation, asymmetry)
sex of the hatched or sexed embryo
candidate_data: The Stoddard et al. (2017) avian egg shape dataset gives shape indices for thousands of species; sex-by-egg-shape data exist only in scattered poultry studies.

label: Hens lay wind-eggs without ever having mated
claim: Hens and geese that have never copulated lay wind-eggs, so wind-eggs are not left-over products of earlier copulation.
quote: we have cases well authenticated where chickens of the common hen and goose have laid wind-eggs without ever having been subjected to copulation
scope: Common hen and goose; wind-eggs (unfertilized eggs)
measurable_quantities: eggs laid by hens kept without males
fertility of those eggs
candidate_data: Commercial egg production and poultry husbandry records show that hens kept without cocks lay unfertilized eggs; the Animal Diversity Web and poultry-science literature document it.

label: Egg and chick generation times scale with the size of the parent bird
claim: The time from copulation to the finished egg, and from the egg to the hatched chick, differs between bird species according to the size of the parent birds.
quote: The generation of the egg after copulation and the generation of the chick from the subsequent hatching of the egg are not brought about within equal periods for all birds, but differ as to time according to the size of the parent-birds.
scope: Birds in general
measurable_quantities: incubation period
body mass
interval from copulation to laying
candidate_data: The Amniote Life-History Database and AVONET give incubation time and body mass for thousands of bird species; copulation-to-laying intervals are scattered in the literature.

label: In the chick embryo the heart appears as a beating speck of blood
claim: In the incubating hen's egg the heart appears early as a speck of blood in the white that beats and moves as if alive.
quote: and the heart appears, like a speck of blood, in the white of the egg. This point beats and moves as though endowed with life
scope: Chick embryo of the common hen (Gallus gallus)
measurable_quantities: developmental stage at which the heart tube forms and begins to beat
candidate_data: Hamburger and Hamilton chick staging tables and embryology references give the timing of heart formation and first heartbeat.

label: The eagle mother expels one of her two young from the nest
claim: As the young eagles grow, the mother tires of feeding them and drives one of the pair out of the nest.
quote: As the young ones grow, the mother becomes wearied with feeding them and extrudes one of the pair from the nest.
scope: Eagles (Aquila and related genera)
measurable_quantities: fate of the second chick
brood reduction rate in eagle nests
who removes the chick
candidate_data: Long-term raptor nest-monitoring studies document brood reduction and siblicide in eagles; Birds of the World species accounts summarise them.

label: The raven lays more than two eggs
claim: The raven lays more than two eggs; the claim that it lays only two is false.
quote: It is not true that, as some aver, the raven lays only two eggs; it lays a larger number.
scope: Raven (Corvus corax)
measurable_quantities: raven clutch size
candidate_data: Clutch-size records for Corvus corax in the Amniote Life-History Database and Birds of the World.

label: The cuckoo lays in smaller birds' nests after eating their eggs
claim: The cuckoo builds no nest but lays its egg in the nest of a smaller bird after first devouring that bird's eggs, preferring the ringdove's nest, and the hypolais hatches and rears its young.
quote: Sometimes it lays its eggs in the nest of a smaller bird after first devouring the eggs of this bird; it lays by preference in the nest of the ringdove, after first devouring the eggs of the pigeon.
scope: Common cuckoo (Cuculus canorus); hosts: ringdove, pigeon, hypolais (warblers)
measurable_quantities: host species list for the cuckoo
frequency of host egg removal by the laying female
doves as hosts
candidate_data: Published cuckoo host records and brood-parasite databases, plus Birds of the World accounts; cuckoo egg-removal behaviour is documented in field studies.

label: Cartilaginous fishes are viviparous and all other fishes oviparous
claim: Cartilaginous fishes (selachians) are viviparous, first oviparous internally and then viviparous, and the rest of the fishes are oviparous; the fishing-frog is the one cartilaginous exception that does not rear its young internally.
quote: Fishes of the cartilaginous genus are viviparous; the rest are oviparous. And cartilaginous fishes are first oviparous internally and subsequently viviparous; they rear the embryos internally, the batrachus or fishing-frog being an exception.
scope: Cartilaginous fishes (sharks, rays, skates) versus other fishes; fishing-frog (a bony fish, Lophius)
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode by fish species (oviparous, viviparous, ovoviviparous)
candidate_data: FishBase and Sharkipedia record reproductive mode for thousands of fish species, including oviparous skates and viviparous bony fishes.

label: The smooth shark's embryo is nourished by a navel-string like a quadruped's
claim: In the smooth shark the embryo develops with its navel-string attached to the womb, so that when the egg substance is used up the embryo is sustained much as in a quadruped.
quote: these eggs shift into each of the two horns of the womb and descend, and the young develop with the navel-string attached to the womb, so that, as the egg-substance gets used up, the embryo is sustained to all appearance just as in the case of quadrupeds.
scope: Smooth shark (Mustelus, likely the smooth-hound)
measurable_quantities: presence of a yolk-sac placenta in Mustelus species
candidate_data: Anatomical and reproductive studies of Mustelus placentation in the primary literature; FishBase records reproductive mode.

label: Smooth shark males develop on the left of the womb and females on the right
claim: In the smooth shark, male embryos are generated on the left side of the womb and females on the right, and both sexes also occur together on the same side.
quote: Males are generated on the left-hand side of the womb, and females on the right-hand side, and males and females on the same side together.
scope: Smooth shark (Mustelus) embryos in the uterus
measurable_quantities: sex of embryos by uterine side in pregnant females
candidate_data: Embryo sex by uterine horn is recorded in fisheries biology studies of pregnant Mustelus; not available in a database.

label: All scaly fishes are oviparous
claim: All scaly fishes, such as the basse, the mullets and the white-fish, are oviparous, as are all smooth or slippery fishes except the eel.
quote: all scaly fish are oviparous, as the basse, the mullet, the grey mullet, and the etelis, and all the so-called white-fish, and all the smooth or slippery fish except the eel
scope: Bony fishes with scales (teleosts: basse, mullets and similar)
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode of scaled teleosts
candidate_data: FishBase reproductive-mode records identify live-bearing teleosts such as poeciliids, which bear on the claim.

label: Only eggs sprinkled by the male's milt produce young fishes
claim: In egg-laying fishes the female deposits her eggs and the male follows and sheds milt over them; only the eggs so sprinkled give young, and the rest are left to their fate.
quote: for when the female has laid her eggs, the male follows and sheds its sperm over them, and from all the eggs so besprinkled young fishes proceed, while the rest are left to their fate.
scope: Oviparous fishes that pair, including river fishes
measurable_quantities: proportion of spawned eggs fertilised
sequence of egg deposition and milt release
candidate_data: External fertilisation in teleost spawning is documented in fisheries and developmental biology literature; FishBase records spawning behaviour.

label: Only the sheat-fish guards its eggs, with the carp as a possible exception
claim: Of all fishes, only the sheat-fish keeps guard over its spawn, except perhaps the carp, which is said to stay on guard if its spawn lies in a solid mass.
quote: For, with the exception of the sheatfish, no fish keeps on guard; unless, by the way, it be the carp, which is said to remain on guard, if it so happen that its spawn lies in a solid mass.
scope: Freshwater fishes (sheat-fish Silurus glanis; carp); fishes in general
measurable_quantities: presence of parental egg guarding by fish species
candidate_data: FishBase reproductive-guild records and comparative reviews of parental care in teleosts show many guarding species, including sticklebacks and gobies.

label: Eels do not pair or lay eggs and have never been found with milt or spawn
claim: Eels are not produced by pairing and are not oviparous; no eel has ever been found with milt or spawn, nor with passages for spawn or eggs when cut open.
quote: Eels are not the issue of pairing, neither are they oviparous; nor was an eel ever found supplied with either milt or spawn, nor are they when cut open found to have within them passages for spawn or for eggs.
scope: Eels (Anguilla, the freshwater eels of the Mediterranean)
measurable_quantities: gonad development and egg production in eels
oviducts in dissected eels
candidate_data: Literature on Anguilla gonad maturation and Sargasso Sea spawning (such as Schmidt 1922) and eel life-history data in FishBase.

label: Some fishes arise spontaneously from mud and sand
claim: Certain fishes come into existence spontaneously from mud, sand and decayed matter, not from eggs or copulation.
quote: From the facts above enumerated it is quite proved that certain fishes come spontaneously into existence, not being derived from eggs or from copulation.
scope: Small fishes of drying ponds and coasts (the Cnidos mullet and the 'froth' fry)
measurable_quantities: reappearance of fish in dried-out ponds after rain
presence of eggs or gonads in the fish found
candidate_data: Studies of annual killifish with drought-resistant eggs, such as Nothobranchius, explain fishes that reappear in dried ponds; no database for the claim itself.

label: Fish gestation always lasts a number of days divisible by seven
claim: The time fishes carry their eggs is at most thirty days and in every species is a number of days divisible by seven.
quote: With some fishes the time of gestation is not longer than thirty days, with others it is a lesser period; but with all it extends over a number of days divisible by seven.
scope: Fishes in general
measurable_quantities: egg-carrying or gestation duration in days for fish species
candidate_data: FishBase gives egg development and spawning-cycle durations for some species; gestation periods are scattered for live-bearers.

label: Cartilaginous fishes are less prolific than other fishes because they are viviparous
claim: Cartilaginous fishes are less prolific than other fishes because they are viviparous, and their young, being larger, are more likely to escape destruction.
quote: As a rule, cartilaginous fish are less prolific than other fish owing to their being viviparous; and their young by reason of their size have a better chance of escaping destruction.
scope: Cartilaginous fishes (sharks and rays) versus other fishes
measurable_quantities: fecundity per female
offspring size
juvenile survival
candidate_data: FishBase fecundity records and Sharkipedia life-history traits for sharks and rays compared with teleosts.

label: Cetaceans are viviparous
claim: The dolphin, the whale and all the other cetaceans, which have a blow-hole instead of gills, are viviparous and produce an embryo rather than eggs.
quote: The dolphin, the whale, and all the rest of the Cetacea, all, that is to say, that are provided with a blow-hole instead of gills, are viviparous.
scope: Cetaceans: dolphin, porpoise, whale
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode of cetacean species
candidate_data: PanTHERIA and AnAge give reproductive traits for cetacean species, and the Animal Diversity Web species accounts record live birth.

label: The dolphin's gestation lasts ten months
claim: The dolphin's period of gestation is ten months.
quote: Its period of gestation is ten months.
scope: Dolphin (Delphinus delphis, the Mediterranean common dolphin)
measurable_quantities: gestation length in months
candidate_data: PanTHERIA and AnAge give gestation length for dolphin species.

label: Females are most cross-tempered after parturition and males at pairing time
claim: Female animals are most cross-tempered just after giving birth, and males are most cross-tempered during the pairing season.
quote: The female is most cross-tempered just after parturition, the male during the time of pairing
scope: Mammals in general: stallions, boars, bulls, rams, camels, bears, wolves, lions
measurable_quantities: aggression by sex and reproductive state
candidate_data: Comparative literature on maternal and rut-season aggression in mammals; no single database codes aggression by reproductive state.

label: Mares in heat flee north or south and never east or west
claim: A mare in the condition of sexual frenzy flees invariably northwards or southwards and never towards the east or the west.
quote: The mares under these circumstances fly invariably either northwards or southwards, and never towards either east or west.
scope: Mares in heat, in Crete and elsewhere
measurable_quantities: compass direction of travel by mares in estrus
candidate_data: GPS or observational studies of free-ranging horse movement; none known that record direction by reproductive state.

label: Sheep and goats bear male young under north winds and female under south winds
claim: If ewes and she-goats mate when north winds are blowing they tend to bear males, and if they mate when south winds are blowing they tend to bear females.
quote: And if they submit to the male when north winds are blowing, they are apt to bear males; if when south winds are blowing, females.
scope: Domestic sheep and goats
measurable_quantities: offspring sex ratio by wind direction at mating
candidate_data: Flock records of lamb sex ratio and meteorological wind records could be linked; large livestock sex-ratio datasets exist in the animal-science literature.

label: The Laconian bitch carries her pups about sixty days and they are blind twelve days
claim: The Laconian hound bitch is pregnant for about sixty days, give or take a few, and her pups are blind for twelve days after birth.
quote: The Laconian bitch carries her young the sixth part of a year or sixty days: or more by one, two, or three, or less by one; the pups are blind for twelve days after birth.
scope: Domestic dog (Canis familiaris), Laconian breed
measurable_quantities: gestation length in days
age at eye opening
candidate_data: AnAge, PanTHERIA and veterinary references give dog gestation (about 63 days) and eye opening; breed-specific data are scattered.

label: Dogs shed no teeth but the canines, at four months
claim: The dog sheds no teeth except the canines, which a dog of either sex sheds at four months old.
quote: The dog sheds no teeth except the so-called 'canines'; these a dog of either sex sheds when four months old.
scope: Domestic dog
measurable_quantities: which teeth are replaced and at what age
candidate_data: Veterinary dental references give the dog's deciduous and permanent eruption schedule.

label: The cow goes with calf nine months and calves in the tenth
claim: The cow is pregnant for nine months and calves in the tenth month.
quote: The cow goes with calf for nine months, and she calves in the tenth month
scope: Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)
measurable_quantities: gestation length in months
candidate_data: AnAge and PanTHERIA give cattle gestation length (about 283 days).

label: A prematurely delivered calf never lives
claim: A calf born before the proper time is an abortion and never lives, however little premature, because its hooves are weak and imperfect.
quote: A calf delivered before the times here specified is an abortion and never lives, however little premature its birth may have been, as its hooves are weak and imperfect.
scope: Domestic cattle
measurable_quantities: survival of calves born before term by days premature
candidate_data: Veterinary studies of calf survival after preterm birth and dairy-herd records of gestation length and neonatal survival.

label: The horse sheds its teeth in sets of four up to four and a half years
claim: A horse sheds its first set of four teeth at two and a half years, a second set after a year and a third a year later, and sheds no more after four years and six months.
quote: It sheds its first set of four, two from the upper jaw and two from the lower, when two and a half years old. After a year's interval, it sheds another set of four in like manner, and another set of four after yet another year's interval; after arriving at the age of four years and six months it sheds no more.
scope: Domestic horse (Equus caballus)
measurable_quantities: age at shedding of deciduous incisors and permanent tooth eruption
candidate_data: Equine dental-eruption tables in veterinary references give the schedule; none are compiled in an open database.

label: The mare alone stands upright to foal, unlike other quadrupeds
claim: Quadrupeds generally lie down to give birth and the young come out sideways, but the mare stands erect and casts her foal in that posture.
quote: Quadrupeds as a rule lie down for parturition, and in consequence the young of them all come out of the womb sideways. The mare, however, when the time for parturition arrives, stands erect and in that posture casts its foal.
scope: Quadrupeds in general; mare in particular
measurable_quantities: birthing posture of mares
fetal presentation in quadrupeds
candidate_data: Equine obstetrics references and foaling-observation studies describe maternal posture; no database exists.

label: A hybrid's gestation period follows the male parent's own species
claim: In a cross between horse and ass, the gestation period depends on the male and is what it would have been had he mated with a female of his own kind.
quote: The period for gestation in the case of a cross depends on the male, and is just what it would have been if the male had had commerce with a female of his own kind.
scope: Mules and hinnies (horse and ass hybrids)
measurable_quantities: gestation length of mule and hinny pregnancies against the sire's and the dam's species norms
candidate_data: Equine breeding records and veterinary literature give mule and hinny gestation lengths; AnAge and PanTHERIA give the parent species norms.

label: Female mules may conceive but do not carry to term, except in Syrophoenicia
claim: A female mule has been known to conceive without the pregnancy ending in birth, and in Syrophoenicia she-mules mate with mules and bear young.
quote: A female mule has been known to be impregnated, but without the impregnation being followed up by parturition. In Syrophoenicia she-mules submit to the mule and bear young
scope: Mules (horse-ass hybrids)
measurable_quantities: reported fertile mule births and pregnancy outcomes
candidate_data: Published case reports and reviews of fertile mules in the veterinary literature; no single open database.

label: The elephant carries her young two and a half to three years
claim: The female elephant carries her young for two and a half years, or according to others for three years.
quote: The female carries her young, according to some accounts, for two and a half years; according to others, for three years
scope: Elephants (Asian elephant Elephas maximus and African elephants)
measurable_quantities: gestation length in months
candidate_data: AnAge and PanTHERIA give elephant gestation (about 22 months).

label: The newborn elephant sucks with its mouth, not its trunk
claim: The young elephant suckles from its mother immediately after birth using the mouth and not the trunk, and can walk and see well at once.
quote: The young one, immediately after birth, sucks the mother, not with its trunk but with the mouth; and can walk about and see distinctly the moment it is born.
scope: Elephant calves
measurable_quantities: suckling mode of elephant calves
age at first walking
candidate_data: Elephant husbandry and field studies, and the Animal Diversity Web account, describe calf suckling and early mobility.

label: Deer are not long-lived because gestation is short and fawns grow fast
claim: Deer are not extremely long-lived, since their short gestation and the rapid growth of the fawn do not point to great longevity.
quote: Fabulous stories are told concerning the longevity of the animal, but the stories have never been verified, and the brevity of the period of gestation and the rapidity of growth in the fawn would not lead one to attribute extreme longevity to this creature.
scope: Deer (the red deer or hind and stag)
measurable_quantities: maximum longevity of deer
gestation length and juvenile growth rate against lifespan across mammals
candidate_data: AnAge and PanTHERIA give maximum longevity, gestation length and growth traits for mammals, including deer.

label: The she-bear carries young thirty days
claim: The she-bear is pregnant for thirty days.
quote: The she-bear goes with young for thirty days.
scope: Bears (Ursus)
measurable_quantities: gestation length (including delayed implantation) in bears
candidate_data: AnAge and PanTHERIA give bear gestation and the Animal Diversity Web covers delayed implantation.

label: The newborn bear cub is smallest in proportion to its mother of any animal
claim: Of all animals, the newborn bear cub is the smallest in proportion to the size of its mother, larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel.
quote: Of all animals the newly born cub of the she bear is the smallest in proportion to the size of the mother; that is to say, it is larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel.
scope: All animals; she-bear and cub
measurable_quantities: neonate mass relative to adult female mass across mammals
candidate_data: PanTHERIA and AnAge give neonate and adult body mass for mammals; marsupials are the obvious rivals for smallest relative birth size.

label: In Europe lions are found only between the Achelous and the Nessus
claim: In the whole of Europe, lions are found only in the strip of land between the rivers Achelous and Nessus.
quote: In fact, in the whole of Europe it is only found in the strip between the rivers Achelous and Nessus.
scope: Lions (Panthera leo) in Europe in Aristotle's time
measurable_quantities: historical and fossil occurrence of lions in Europe by region
candidate_data: The Paleobiology Database and GBIF fossil and occurrence records of Panthera leo, plus ancient historical sources.

label: Hyenas are not hermaphrodites and the female's false organ has no duct
claim: Hyenas are not hermaphrodites; the female has a true womb and a male-like part under the tail that is unprovided with duct or passage.
quote: The fact is that the sexual organ of the male hyena resembles the same organ in the wolf and in the dog; the part resembling the female genital organ lies underneath the tail, and does to some extent resemble the female organ, but it is unprovided with duct or passage, and the passage for the residuum comes underneath it.
scope: Hyenas (the spotted hyena Crocuta crocuta is the likely referent)
measurable_quantities: presence of a urogenital canal in the female hyena's external genitalia
candidate_data: Anatomical studies of the female spotted hyena's genital morphology, such as published dissection and imaging work.

label: Hares superfoetate and bear young every month
claim: Hares breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, and bear young every month.
quote: They breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, and bear young every month.
scope: Hares (Lepus)
measurable_quantities: breeding season length
occurrence of superfetation
litter interval in days
candidate_data: Lagomorph reproduction studies in the primary literature; PanTHERIA gives litters per year.

label: Hare young are born blind
claim: The young of the hare are born blind, as is the case with most fissipeds (toed animals).
quote: The young are born blind, as is the case with the greater part Of the fissipeds or toed animals.
scope: Hares; fissipeds (carnivorans with separate toes)
measurable_quantities: eye state at birth in hares
eye state at birth across carnivorans
candidate_data: Life-history references describe leverets as precocial and eyes open at birth; the Animal Diversity Web covers the hare, and PanTHERIA does not record eye state.

label: A pregnant mouse shut in a jar produced over a hundred and twenty mice
claim: A pregnant female mouse accidentally shut in a jar of millet was found, after a little while, to have more than a hundred and twenty mice inside it.
quote: On one occasion a she-mouse in a state of pregnancy was shut up by accident in a jar containing millet-seed, and after a little while the lid of the jar was removed and upwards of one hundred and twenty mice were found inside it.
scope: House mouse (Mus musculus), one reported instance
measurable_quantities: litter size, gestation period and age at first breeding of mice
maximum offspring from one female over a short period
candidate_data: AnAge and PanTHERIA give mouse litter size, gestation and maturity, from which the maximum descendants in a short interval can be computed.
